key_insight: Egocentric human video can be a more scalable and surprisingly stronger pretraining source than real-robot teleoperation data for embodied models. The paper argues that human video can better overcome the data bottleneck while preserving useful behavior and interaction signals.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the scarcity, high cost, and low diversity of real-robot trajectories used for embodied pretraining. It explores whether large-scale human video can replace or outperform expensive robot-collected data.
method: Compare egocentric human video against teleoperated real-robot data as pretraining sources for embodied foundation models.
Leverage large-scale human video to capture diverse actions, scenes, and interactions at much lower collection cost.
Evaluate whether human video pretraining can transfer effectively to embodied tasks despite weaker or less explicit action supervision.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a cheaper and more scalable path to pretraining embodied agents without relying solely on costly robot data collection. It could accelerate dataset building and model development for robotics and embodied AI.

paper_title: HumanScale: Egocentric Human Video Can Outperform Real-Robot Data for Embodied Pretraining
paper_authors: Juncheng Ma, Jianxin Bi, Yufan Deng, Xuanran Zhai, Kewei Zhang
